title: Duchy of Łęczyca
capsule: The Duchy of Łęczyca was a Piast appanage in central Poland centred on the town of Łęczyca, whose separate identity as a distinct duchy emerged from the partitions following Bolesław III Wrymouth's testament of 1138. The 1139–1147 attestation window reflects its earliest appearance as a discrete political unit under the Piast fragmentation; the duchy had a longer intermittent history until 1352, when the last duke died and the territory was reabsorbed into the re-unified Kingdom of Poland. The region remained significant as the site of the Synod of Łęczyca (1180), which shaped Polish ecclesiastical autonomy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. As a Piast duchy documented in medieval Polish chronicles, its core territory is well established; boundaries relative to contemporaneous Mazovian and Kuyavian holdings are less precisely known.
